`crlReloadingFailedCallback` is not for testing - https://github.com/grpc/proposal/blob/dddf32d0116376dd0c48adee7b0071a20bc82b5b/A69-crl-enhancements.md#provider-implementation---directory-provider
`Particularly in the case of updating CRLs, we don't want to error and crash the server if there is a bad update. However, we still want this error to be known, so we will have an optional and overridable error callback when CRLs fail to be read. This will let users tie in whatever alerting/monitoring they may want in these failure cases. This callback will be for notifications/alerting, it will not be a decision-making callback`
I'm fine with whatever.  Even this is acceptable.  I'm just trying to point out things I see that don't look as good as they could be.

It would be even nicer to add documentation and/or scripts where they don't exist, rather than create a new directory where things are better.  Unless you're taking an AI to do that as a cleanup.

Different filenames is fine.  I just know creating new directories for data files incurs an extra cost on our import process, and using data files is different in OSS vs. internally.  So I'd rather avoid it.

return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read %q: %v", path, err)
